overall: The AG found no Open Meeting Law violation: the 'Open Forum' item and the outside attorney's remarks were not reasonably anticipated by the chair, though it recommended postponing significant new topics where possible.

allegations.summary: Complaint alleged the 'Open Forum' agenda item was posted less than 48 hours before the February 6, 2019 meeting.
allegations.key_passage: The Chair also did not reasonably anticipate that Attorney Pill would speak about the VGG project at the time that the meeting notice was amended at 9:35am on February 6.

allegations.summary: Complaint alleged the 'Open Forum' agenda topic was overly vague and did not reasonably inform the public of what would be discussed.
allegations.key_passage: Here, we find that the “Open Lorum” was truly guided by public questions and comments.

allegations.summary: Complaint alleged the Chair invited a speaker whose remarks were not noticed on the agenda.
allegations.key_passage: We have previously stated that the Open Meeting Law does not require the chair of a public body to guess what will occur at a meeting.

note: Read by a language model from the letter; every key passage is checked verbatim against it and dropped if not. A holding is the Attorney General’s reading of the law in this case only.
